questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me, that the university offered courses, that I found interesting. Furthermore, I wanted to go somewhere in Europe with a great school. Lastly, I wanted to improve my german, why Germany of course was the obvious choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend all students to do it! It is an experience for life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The university of Mannheim was absolutely incredible during the whole process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a lot of assistance. We could attend an introweek, where they held a lot of meetings both revolving physical stuff like where is the cafeteria, library and how to get books at the library, where to find school counselling and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again, the University of Mannheim is incredible and very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. We go information on how to find accommodation through the "Studierendenwerk" (studieboliger) and also how we could find something on our own. We got so many helpful informations, why finding accommodation was never something I was stressed about.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in what they call "Ulmenweg" which is the student accommodation, that is located a little outside the citycentre. I was kind of stressed about this at the beginning, but fear not - the public transportation in Mannheim is very good, and the tramstop was right outside the accommodation!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Even though it seems a bit dirty and old when first arriving at Ulmenweg, there is some kind of special vibe to it. A lot of incoming students lived there, and everybody was just in it together!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, the University is very helpful, and it was so easy. I only experienced once or twice that I hadn't fully understood what to do, and then I just asked them per e-mail, and had an answer immediately.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We just forwarded and e-mail explaining first and second priority of courses, and then a few weeks later, we either got it confirmed or denied. I did not hear about anyone not getting their priority.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always e-mail the team, both the general team of the University of Mannheim and also the departemental exchange coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my first priority, so very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to check your e-mail, so you know when to do what.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University of Mannheim provides with professors that are really competent, and extremely passionate about their subject areas. They are very dedicated to communicate their knowledge in the best possible way to the students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was equivalent to the level at UCPH. The only thing I was struggling a bit with in the beginning, was studying in english. We only have one mandatory english course on the bachelors of Law, why I wasn't really familiar with academic law in english. However, this came to me very fast, and everything went very well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It compared fine, I would say. The only thing was that some of the professors used the "harpun-metod", where they just point out a student, and want them to answer. But for me this was fine in the end, even though I usually hate it. I still don't prefer it, but you get used to it. Furthermore, it is not all the professors, that do this. Also we are used to work in groups on the Bachelors of law at UCPH, but this was not something I really did during my semester at the University of Mannheim. I do not know if this was due to covid, or just because they do not use it in the courses I attended.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to German Constitutional Law
An Introduction to the Law and Legal System of the United States
International Arbitration 
EU Fundamental Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the courses I followed were really interesting and I would recommend all of them. I think that you really should choose the Constitutional Law course since it makes sense to study the Constitution of Germany now that you are there. It was also super interesting to get an introduction to how things work in the United States also since UCPH doesn't really provide with a similar course. The professor was a lawyer from the US, and she was just straight up cool. The professor in EU Fundamental Rights was one of the most competent people I have ever met. She works for the Commission, and so she has a lot of practical experience. This course also provides you with very different and new knowledge compared to what you get from the mandatory course EU-law at UCPH. I love the area of procedure so International Arbitration was an obvious choice for me. Again the professor was very talented. So, I would really recommend all of them!

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I did not encounter any unexpected costs. 
And I just want to add that the personal spending was on travling. Furthermore, I normal do not use this many money on food, but I just ate out all the time because it was so cheap!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was a little surprise with how cheap food was.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University of Mannheim provides with like 100 different things that you can do! Extremely many sports etc. You could even play quidditch! The gym was available for free, you could do yoga, soccer, running, dancing - like every sport I know (almost) you could do. There were also some different students club, that you could attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really get to involve that much in student clubs or other sports than the gym, but I would totally recommend you to do that, since it sounded super cool!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mannheim has the perfect location! You can travel by an ICE train and be in Paris by 3 hours! Other than that there are so many beautiful small cities close to Mannheim like Heidelberg, Weinheim, Karlsruhe and Heppenheim. Also if you have the chance, I would recommend you to travel to Munich (and attend Oktoberfest if possible) and then from there travel to Berchtesgarden - it is close to the boarder of Austria and it is absolutely stunning!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Of course there are some differences but the Germans are very kind!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I shared a flat with a local student, so for me that was kind of easy. But other than that just attend the student clubs or do stuff that the University provides for you. For me I was mostly together with incoming students, so I don't know if I specifically have any tips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I actually did not find anything in relation to the German culture very challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Well the Germans are very sweet and helpful!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to check your e-mail - they provide you with all you need to know there!
2. If possible live in a student accommodation! It is a very easy and cool way to meet knew people!
3. Buy a semesterticket via the University - it is not expensive and you can travel very far with it! (kind of like ungdomskort)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not specifically the University, but do not be put off by Germany's slightly old-fashioned way of life. In many places you can only pay with cash, and you have to go down physically and register in the municipality. But it's easy enough once you get used to it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is hard for me to choose. But I would say the academic outcome, the personal outcome and all of the people I met. I have learned so many things about other cultures and I have met the most amazing people. It is very hard to describe in words here, but trust me - it is amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
For me it was probably adjusting to talk and read in english, but again I think I adjusted kind of fast, so I wouldn't call it a challenge. 
I'm like an extroverted introvert so I really need my time alone to get some energy for more socializing. However, I also love being with people all the time. So for me it was a little hard to find the balance of really wanna go to hang out with people, but also to be able to make sure that I got the rest that I need.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I cannot say how much I recommend going to Mannheim. It is fantastic University, they communicate well and also in english! You are in the heart of southern Germany so it is really easy to travel. Now I know that you also do exchange for the academic outcome, but remember to live and enjoy the fact that you easily and also kind of cheap can travel!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
